properties.name: management.health.jms.enabled
properties.description: Whether to enable JMS health check.

properties.name: spring.jms.cache.consumers
properties.description: Whether to cache message consumers.

properties.name: spring.jms.cache.enabled
properties.description: Whether to cache sessions.

properties.name: spring.jms.cache.producers
properties.description: Whether to cache message producers.

properties.name: spring.jms.cache.session-cache-size
properties.description: Size of the session cache (per JMS Session type).

properties.name: spring.jms.client-id
properties.description: Client id of the connection.

properties.name: spring.jms.jndi-name
properties.description: Connection factory JNDI name. When set, takes precedence to others connection factory auto-configurations.

properties.name: spring.jms.listener.auto-startup
properties.description: Start the container automatically on startup.

properties.name: spring.jms.listener.max-concurrency
properties.description: Maximum number of concurrent consumers.

properties.name: spring.jms.listener.max-messages-per-task
properties.description: Maximum number of messages to process in one task. By default, unlimited unless a SchedulingTaskExecutor is configured on the listener (10 messages), as it indicates a preference for short-lived tasks.

properties.name: spring.jms.listener.min-concurrency
properties.description: Minimum number of concurrent consumers. When max-concurrency is not specified the minimum will also be used as the maximum.

properties.name: spring.jms.listener.receive-timeout
properties.description: Timeout to use for receive calls. Use -1 for a no-wait receive or 0 for no timeout at all. The latter is only feasible if not running within a transaction manager and is generally discouraged since it prevents clean shutdown.

properties.name: spring.jms.listener.session.acknowledge-mode
properties.description: Acknowledge mode of the listener container.

properties.name: spring.jms.listener.session.transacted
properties.description: Whether the listener container should use transacted JMS sessions. Defaults to false in the presence of a JtaTransactionManager and true otherwise.

properties.name: spring.jms.pub-sub-domain
properties.description: Whether the default destination type is topic.

properties.name: spring.jms.subscription-durable
properties.description: Whether the subscription is durable.

properties.name: spring.jms.template.default-destination
properties.description: Default destination to use on send and receive operations that do not have a destination parameter.

properties.name: spring.jms.template.delivery-delay
properties.description: Delivery delay to use for send calls.

properties.name: spring.jms.template.delivery-mode
properties.description: Delivery mode. Enables QoS (Quality of Service) when set.

properties.name: spring.jms.template.priority
properties.description: Priority of a message when sending. Enables QoS (Quality of Service) when set.

properties.name: spring.jms.template.qos-enabled
properties.description: Whether to enable explicit QoS (Quality of Service) when sending a message. When enabled, the delivery mode, priority and time-to-live properties will be used when sending a message. QoS is automatically enabled when at least one of those settings is customized.

properties.name: spring.jms.template.receive-timeout
properties.description: Timeout to use for receive calls.

properties.name: spring.jms.template.session.acknowledge-mode
properties.description: Acknowledge mode used when creating sessions.

properties.name: spring.jms.template.session.transacted
properties.description: Whether to use transacted sessions.

properties.name: spring.jms.template.time-to-live
properties.description: Time-to-live of a message when sending. Enables QoS (Quality of Service) when set.

values.description: Messages sent or received from the session are automatically acknowledged. This is the simplest mode and enables once-only message delivery guarantee.

Messages are acknowledged once the message listener implementation has called "jakarta.jms.Message#acknowledge()". This mode gives the application (rather than the JMS provider) complete control over message acknowledgement.
Similar to auto acknowledgment except that said acknowledgment is lazy. As a consequence, the messages might be delivered more than once. This mode enables at-least-once message delivery guarantee.
